name: Axon Framework
license: Apache 2.0; the Axoniq Framework modules on top of it are commercial and need a subscription for production
summary: A Java framework, not a database, for building event-sourced applications with CQRS and domain-driven design: commands, events and queries as messages, plus an event store to keep the events in.
intro: Axon Framework is a library you add to a JVM application. It is not a database: it gives you the building blocks for domain-driven design, CQRS and event sourcing, namely entities, command, event and query buses, an event store abstraction, event processors and test fixtures, and stores the events through a storage engine you configure. Its makers say its main feature is location transparency: components only exchange messages, so a handler can move to another service without its callers changing.

An event-sourced entity keeps no state of its own in a table. Command handlers check a command against the current state and append events; event sourcing handlers, which may only assign fields, apply those events. Because the same handlers run again whenever the entity is loaded from its events, any business logic in them would run again on every load. Axon Framework 5 replaced the fixed aggregate stream with a Dynamic Consistency Boundary: events carry tags, one event can belong to several entities, and a consistency marker makes an append fail if matching events were written after the state was read.

Axoniq also sells Axon Server, an event store and message router for commands, events and queries. Since Axon Framework 5.1, connecting to Axon Server, a PostgreSQL-optimised event store and durable workflows that replace the old sagas are commercial Axoniq Framework modules; the open-source core stores events per entity through JPA.
strengths: The open-source core is Apache 2.0 and free in production, covering messaging, entity modelling, event sourcing and test fixtures
Commands, events and queries are messages, so components can be split into separate services later without rewriting their callers
Dynamic Consistency Boundaries let one command decide over events from several entities, with conflicting writes still detected
Fits Spring Boot: annotate an entity with `@EventSourced` and auto-configuration registers it
limits: Much of what production systems need is in paid Axoniq Framework modules: Axon Server connectivity, PostgreSQL-optimised storage, sequenced dead-letter queues and workflows

Axoniq Framework modules check their subscription at runtime: without credentials they run for 15 minutes, and without a connection to Axoniq Platform for 24 hours, before shutting the application down
Version 5 is a large break from 4: sagas are gone and aggregates become entities, so upgrades follow a migration guide
The open-source core defines only the snapshot storage API; you write the implementation or buy the Axoniq one

record EnrollStudentCommand(@TargetEntityId String courseId, String studentId) {}  // which course to load
record CourseCreatedEvent(@EventTag String courseId, String title, int capacity) {}
record StudentEnrolledEvent(@EventTag String courseId, String studentId) {}
public static String handle(CreateCourseCommand cmd, EventAppender events) {
if (cmd.capacity() <= 0) throw new IllegalArgumentException("Capacity must be positive");
@CommandHandler  // runs on the state rebuilt from this course's events
public void handle(EnrollStudentCommand cmd, EventAppender events) {
if (enrolledCount >= capacity) throw new IllegalStateException("Course is full");
@EventSourcingHandler  // only assigns state: it runs again on every replay
private void on(CourseCreatedEvent e) { courseId = e.courseId(); capacity = e.capacity(); }

story: Allard Buijze, a software architect who specialised in scalability, started Axon Framework as open source in 2009. Recurring performance and flexibility problems had convinced him that applications needed a solid domain model, and Axon put the ideas of domain-driven design, CQRS and event sourcing into building blocks for Java.

In July 2017 Buijze and Jeroen Speekenbrink founded AxonIQ (now written Axoniq) to work only on Axon. That year it released AxonHub, a message router that knew the difference between commands, events and queries, and early in 2018 AxonDB, a purpose-built event store. At the 2018 Event-Driven Microservices Conference, where Buijze said the framework had passed one million downloads, the two were merged into Axon Server, offered as open source and as an enterprise version.

Axon Framework 5.0, released in November 2025, replaced the aggregate-centred event store with Dynamic Consistency Boundaries. From 5.1 in 2026, the project split in two: Axon Framework stays Apache 2.0, and Axoniq Framework adds commercial modules such as Axon Server connectivity and workflows.

choices.why: Buijze argued that the primary feature of Axon is not CQRS but that components don’t know where each other run, so a well-structured monolith can later be split into services without rewriting it.

choices.choice: Events as the source of truth, with handlers kept apart
choices.why: An entity is rebuilt by replaying its events, so the code that applies events may only assign state, and all decisions live in command handlers that append new events.

choices.choice: Dynamic Consistency Boundaries instead of one stream per aggregate
choices.why: Tags let an event belong to several entities and let a command read all the events it needs, while a consistency marker still rejects an append if a conflicting event arrived in between.

choices.choice: An open-source core with paid modules
choices.why: The Apache 2.0 core covers messaging, modelling and event sourcing; production-grade storage, distribution and workflows are sold by subscription as Axoniq Framework.

timeline.text: Allard Buijze starts Axon Framework as open source
AxonIQ is founded in July and releases AxonHub
AxonHub and the AxonDB event store merge into Axon Server
Axon Framework 5.0 introduces Dynamic Consistency Boundaries
5.1 adds the commercial Axoniq Framework modules on top of the open-source core
